title: Linking through unique identifiers in video metadata
description: Video clips uploaded from Home Hub likely contain metadata with unique identifiers (device ID, user account, timestamps) that can link video data to specific individuals or households.
assumptions: Video metadata includes identifiable information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of video content attributes (location, time, people visible) with metadata can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Video content combined with metadata creates linkable profile

title: Processing of identified personal data
description: Video clips are personal data that identifies individuals in the home environment, and this data is being processed for cloud storage.
assumptions: Video content contains identifiable people

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content reveals revealing attributes about data subjects including appearance, activities, location, and context that support identification.
assumptions: Video captures identifiable activities and attributes

title: Small anonymity set allows singling out
description: In a home context, the number of people visible in video is small, making it easy to single out specific individuals from the video content.
assumptions: Home video typically shows limited number of individuals

title: Highly sensitive data type collected
description: Video footage is highly sensitive personal data that captures private activities and should only be collected when strictly required.
assumptions: Video is considered sensitive personal data

title: Data propagation to cloud services
description: Video data is propagated to cloud storage services where it may be accessible by additional parties beyond the immediate user.
assumptions: Cloud storage involves third-party service providers

title: Excessive party exposure to personal data
description: Video data made accessible to cloud storage provider and potentially their sub-processors, exceeding what may be functionally necessary.
assumptions: Cloud storage involves multiple service tiers and partners

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware that their video is being recorded, uploaded, and stored in the cloud.
assumptions: Users may not understand full data processing chain

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: Users may have limited ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, stored, and potentially shared.
assumptions: User consent mechanisms may be limited

title: Difficulty rectifying or erasing video data
description: Users may lack control to easily rectify incorrect data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant from cloud storage.
assumptions: Cloud storage retention policies may be inflexible

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data collection may process more personal data than actually needed for the functional goal of home security monitoring.
assumptions: Full video recording may exceed minimal necessary data

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video data may be stored longer than functionally needed, potentially exceeding legal retention requirements.
assumptions: Cloud storage retention may not align with legal requirements

title: Linking through unique identifier in notification
description: The motion-detected notification contains the homeowner's unique identifier (e.g., phone number, user ID) to route to the correct device, enabling linking of notification data to a specific individual.
assumptions: Notification includes user identifier for routing

title: Profiling individual through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection data can be analyzed to profile individual behavior patterns (e.g., when homeowner is home/away, daily routines), enabling inference of personal information.
assumptions: Motion data is collected and stored for analysis

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes identified data (homeowner's notification preferences, contact information) to deliver motion-detected alerts to the correct user.
assumptions: Homeowner identity is known and processed

title: Revealing attributes through motion detection
description: Motion detection data reveals revealing attributes about the homeowner's presence, location, and daily routines, supporting identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion data indicates presence/absence at property

title: Detecting through observed communications
description: The notification itself reveals that motion was detected at the property, making the detection observable to the homeowner and potentially others.
assumptions: Notification delivery confirms motion event occurred

title: Excessive data type granularity
description: The notification may reveal more granular information about motion events (time, location, intensity) than functionally needed for a simple alert.
assumptions: Notification includes detailed motion metadata

title: Implicit data disclosure through notification
description: Motion detection data is implicitly disclosed as a side-effect of the notification flow, revealing patterns about homeowner's daily routine and presence.
assumptions: Notification reveals motion patterns beyond explicit intent

title: Unawareness of motion detection processing
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware that motion detection is actively processing their property data and sending notifications.
assumptions: User may not understand full scope of motion detection

title: Lack of control over notification preferences
description: Homeowner may lack control to customize which motion events trigger notifications, how frequently, or to disable motion detection entirely.
assumptions: Limited user control over notification settings

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Motion detection data may be processed beyond what is functionally needed for sending a simple notification, potentially collecting more data than required.
assumptions: System collects more motion data than necessary for alert functionality

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The video clip stored in the cloud is identified data associated with a specific homeowner, and is being retrieved and processed by the mobile app backend for playback.

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content inherently reveals personal attributes about the homeowner (location, activities, environment, etc.) which supports identification of the data subject.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be perceived as more sensitive than strictly required for simple playback functionality.

title: Potential unnecessary video processing
description: The video may be processed, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is functionally needed for simple playback (e.g., metadata extraction, content analysis).

title: Video accessible to multiple parties
description: The video data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., cloud storage providers, app backend, potentially third parties).

title: Homeowner unawareness of video processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of how their video data is being processed, stored, or potentially disclosed beyond simple playback.

title: Lack of homeowner control over video processing
description: The homeowner may lack control over preferences regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or retained.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the playback functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.

title: Video data propagation to other services
description: The mobile app backend may propagate video data to other services where it is not needed (e.g., analytics, sharing features, cloud sync).

title: Lack of homeowner access control
description: The homeowner may lack adequate control in accessing or managing the video data that is being processed by the mobile app backend.
